# ISO 27001:2022 Gap Analysis & Readiness Roadmap
**Profile:** ~250 employees, financial services, ITIL-aligned operations, no formal ISMS

**How to use this:** Status ratings are my assumptions from your description. Verify each one with evidence before relying on it.

- ✅ Likely in place (needs formal evidence)
- 🟡 Partial
- ❌ Gap
- **P1** = blocks certification, **P2** = high risk or high audit focus in financial services, **P3** = important but can follow

---

## Part 1: Management System Clauses (4–10)

These are mandatory. Auditors check every one, and you can't exclude any. Since you have no ISMS, this is where most of your work lies.

| Clause | Requirement | Status | ITIL link | Gap / Action | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **4.1** | Context: internal and external issues (incl. climate change per Amd 1:2024) | ❌ | Strategy management | Document issues: regulatory, threat landscape, outsourcing, growth plans | P1 |
| **4.2** | Interested parties and their requirements | ❌ | Relationship management | List regulators, customers, auditors, and key vendors. Build a **legal/regulatory register** (e.g., GLBA, NYDFS 500, DORA, PCI DSS, whichever apply) | P1 |
| **4.3** | ISMS scope (documented) | ❌ | Service catalogue | Define scope: org units, locations, services, systems, interfaces. Use the service catalogue as the starting point | P1 |
| **4.4** | Establish, implement, maintain, and improve the ISMS | ❌ | — | Outcome of this whole program | P1 |
| **5.1** | Leadership and commitment | ❌ | — | Named executive sponsor, ISMS on exec/board agenda | P1 |
| **5.2** | Information security policy (documented) | 🟡 | — | Top-level policy approved by management, with objectives and a commitment to improvement | P1 |
| **5.3** | Roles, responsibilities, authorities | 🟡 | Practice owners | Assign ISMS owner, risk owners, control owners. Draft a RACI | P1 |
| **6.1.1** | Actions to address risks and opportunities | ❌ | — | Covered by 6.1.2 and 6.1.3 | P1 |
| **6.1.2** | Risk assessment process (documented) | ❌ | Risk management | Define methodology: asset- or scenario-based, likelihood/impact scales, acceptance criteria | P1 |
| **6.1.3** | Risk treatment plus **Statement of Applicability** | ❌ | — | Treatment plan with owners and dates. SoA covering all 93 Annex A controls with justification | P1 |
| **6.2** | Security objectives (measurable) | ❌ | Measurement & reporting | 5–8 objectives, e.g., "critical patches within 14 days ≥95%" | P1 |
| **6.3** | Planning of changes to the ISMS | ❌ | Change enablement | Extend your change process to ISMS changes | P2 |
| **7.1** | Resources | 🟡 | Workforce mgmt | Budget and FTE for ISMS operation | P1 |
| **7.2** | Competence (documented evidence) | 🟡 | Workforce mgmt | Skills matrix and training records for security roles | P2 |
| **7.3** | Awareness | 🟡 | — | See Annex A 6.3 | P2 |
| **7.4** | Communication | ❌ | Relationship mgmt | Communication plan: what, when, to whom, by whom | P3 |
| **7.5** | Documented information control | 🟡 | Knowledge mgmt | Document control: versioning, approval, review cycle, retention | P1 |
| **8.1** | Operational planning and control | 🟡 | Change, release, supplier | Show processes run as designed, incl. outsourced processes | P1 |
| **8.2** | Perform risk assessments (results retained) | ❌ | — | Initial assessment, then at planned intervals and on significant change | P1 |
| **8.3** | Implement risk treatment (results retained) | ❌ | — | Track treatment progress | P1 |
| **9.1** | Monitoring and measurement (results retained) | 🟡 | Measurement & reporting | Use your existing ITIL KPIs; add security metrics | P1 |
| **9.2** | Internal audit (programme and results) | ❌ | — | Audit programme. Auditor must be independent of the area audited; outsourcing is fine | P1 |
| **9.3** | Management review (results retained) | ❌ | Continual improvement | At least one full review with all required inputs before certification | P1 |
| **10.1** | Continual improvement | 🟡 | Continual improvement | Use the ITIL CI register for ISMS improvements | P2 |
| **10.2** | Nonconformity and corrective action | 🟡 | Problem management | Use problem management for root cause. Log ISMS nonconformities | P1 |

**Key leverage:** ITIL **problem management** and **continual improvement** map closely to Clause 10. **Change enablement** covers 6.3 and 8.1. Formalize them rather than building parallel processes.

---

## Part 2: Annex A Controls (by theme)

Your SoA must address **all 93 controls**. The table below covers the ones most relevant to your stated environment and to financial-services audits. The remaining controls still need an SoA entry, but they're usually lower effort (many physical controls, for example, may be largely handled by your landlord or data center).

### 5. Organizational Controls (37)

| Control | Status | ITIL practice | Gap / Action | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 Policies for information security | 🟡 | — | Build a policy hierarchy: top-level policy plus topic policies (access, crypto, backup, acceptable use, etc.). Approve, publish, and review annually | P1 |
| 5.2–5.4 Roles, segregation of duties, management responsibilities | 🟡 | Practice owners | SoD matrix for finance systems, admin roles, and change approvals | P2 |
| 5.5–5.6 Contact with authorities and special interest groups | ❌ | — | Regulator and law-enforcement contacts; FS-ISAC or equivalent membership | P3 |
| **5.7 Threat intelligence** *(new in 2022)* | ❌ | Monitoring & event mgmt | Feed threat intel into SIEM and risk assessment (FS-ISAC, vendor feeds) | P2 |
| 5.8 Security in project management | ❌ | Project mgmt / Change | Add a security checkpoint to project gates and normal or major changes | P2 |
| **5.9 Inventory of information and assets** | 🟡 | **Service configuration mgmt** | **CMDB is partial.** Complete it for in-scope assets with owner, classification, and location. Doesn't need to be perfect, but must be reliable for scope | **P1** |
| 5.10 Acceptable use | 🟡 | — | AUP acknowledged by all staff | P2 |
| 5.11 Return of assets | 🟡 | Service request / HR | Offboarding checklist with asset return evidence | P2 |
| 5.12–5.13 Classification and labelling | ❌ | — | 3–4 level scheme (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted), applied to customer and financial data | P2 |
| 5.14 Information transfer | 🟡 | — | Rules for email, file transfer, and removable media | P3 |
| **5.15–5.18 Access control, identity, authentication, access rights** | 🟡 | Service request mgmt, Info security mgmt | Formal joiner-mover-leaver process, **periodic access reviews** (quarterly for privileged and financial systems), MFA policy | **P1** |
| **5.19–5.22 Supplier security** | ❌ (ad-hoc) | **Supplier management** | Supplier inventory, criticality tiering, due-diligence questionnaire, contract security clauses, annual review of critical vendors. **Heavy regulatory focus in financial services** | **P1** |
| **5.23 Cloud services** *(new)* | ❌ | Supplier mgmt | Cloud acquisition, use, and exit process. Shared responsibility documented | P2 |
| **5.24–5.28 Incident management** | ✅/🟡 | **Incident management** | ITIL incident exists. Add security incident classification, playbooks, evidence collection (5.28), lessons learned (5.27), and **regulatory notification timelines** | **P1** |
| 5.29 Security during disruption | 🟡 | Service continuity | Security maintained in DR mode | P2 |
| **5.30 ICT readiness for business continuity** *(new)* | 🟡 | **Service continuity mgmt** | BIA, RTO/RPO per service, **tested** DR plans with results recorded | **P1** |
| **5.31 Legal, statutory, regulatory, contractual requirements** | ❌ | — | Regulatory register (ties to 4.2) | **P1** |
| 5.32 Intellectual property rights | 🟡 | Software asset mgmt | License compliance | P3 |
| **5.33 Protection of records** | 🟡 | — | Retention schedule aligned to financial regulations. **This drives your log retention decision** | P2 |
| 5.34 Privacy and PII | 🟡 | — | Align with privacy program (GLBA/GDPR/state laws as applicable) | P2 |
| 5.35 Independent review of infosec | ❌ | — | Internal audit or external review | P1 |
| 5.36 Compliance with policies and standards | ❌ | — | Periodic compliance checks | P2 |
| 5.37 Documented operating procedures | 🟡 | Knowledge mgmt | ITIL procedures likely exist. Make sure they're controlled and current | P2 |

### 6. People Controls (8)

| Control | Status | ITIL practice | Gap / Action | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 Screening | 🟡 | Workforce mgmt | Likely done for regulatory reasons in FS. Document it, risk-based by role | P2 |
| 6.2 Terms and conditions of employment | 🟡 | — | Security responsibilities in contracts | P3 |
| **6.3 Awareness, education, training** | 🟡 | Workforce mgmt | Annual training, phishing simulations, completion tracking (≥95% target) | **P1** |
| 6.4 Disciplinary process | 🟡 | — | Referenced in policy | P3 |
| 6.5 Responsibilities after termination | 🟡 | — | Confidentiality obligations survive termination | P3 |
| 6.6 Confidentiality / NDAs | 🟡 | — | NDA register | P3 |
| 6.7 Remote working | 🟡 | — | Remote work policy and technical controls | P2 |
| 6.8 Security event reporting | 🟡 | Service desk / Incident | Clear "how to report" channel for staff | P2 |

### 7. Physical Controls (14)

Usually lighter work for a 250-person office. Confirm data center or colocation coverage via supplier assurance (e.g., SOC 2 reports).

| Control | Status | Gap / Action | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.1–7.6 Perimeters, entry, secure areas | 🟡 | Badge access logs, visitor log, server/comms room restrictions | P3 |
| **7.4 Physical security monitoring** *(new)* | 🟡 | CCTV or alarm coverage documented | P3 |
| 7.7 Clear desk / clear screen | ❌ | Policy plus spot checks | P3 |
| 7.8–7.13 Equipment siting, utilities, cabling, maintenance | 🟡 | Mostly facilities or provider evidence | P3 |
| **7.10 Storage media** / **7.14 Secure disposal** | 🟡 | Disposal certificates, encryption of removable media | P2 |

### 8. Technological Controls (34)

| Control | Status | ITIL practice | Gap / Action | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8.1 User endpoint devices | 🟡 | — | MDM, disk encryption, EDR coverage report | P2 |
| **8.2 Privileged access** | 🟡 | Info security mgmt | PAM or vaulting, separate admin accounts, quarterly review | **P1** |
| 8.3 Information access restriction | 🟡 | — | Least privilege on file shares and apps | P2 |
| 8.5 Secure authentication | 🟡 | — | MFA on remote access, email, admin, and financial apps | **P1** |
| 8.7 Protection against malware | ✅ | — | Evidence of coverage | P3 |
| **8.8 Technical vulnerability management** | ✅/🟡 | **Deployment / Release mgmt** | **Weekly patching is a good base.** Add: authenticated vuln scanning, **risk-based remediation SLAs** (e.g., critical ≤14 days, high ≤30), exception process, annual pen test | **P1** |
| **8.9 Configuration management** *(new)* | 🟡 | **Service config mgmt** | Secure baselines (e.g., CIS Benchmarks) and drift monitoring. Different from the CMDB but related | P2 |
| **8.10 Information deletion** *(new)* | ❌ | — | Deletion per retention schedule | P3 |
| **8.11 Data masking** *(new)* | ❌ | — | Mask customer data in non-production environments | P2 |
| **8.12 Data leakage prevention** *(new)* | ❌/🟡 | — | DLP for email and endpoints, risk-based | P2 |
| **8.13 Information backup** | 🟡 | Service continuity | Backup policy, **immutable/offline copies**, documented restore tests | **P1** |
| 8.14 Redundancy | 🟡 | Availability mgmt | Aligned to BIA | P2 |
| **8.15 Logging** | 🟡 | Monitoring & event mgmt | **90-day retention:** ISO doesn't set a period, but your regulatory register (5.31/5.33) will. Many FS regimes and PCI DSS expect ≥1 year, with recent logs readily available. Consider 90 days hot plus 12+ months archive. Protect logs from tampering | **P1** |
| **8.16 Monitoring activities** *(new)* | ✅/🟡 | Monitoring & event mgmt | SIEM exists. Document use cases, alert triage, and coverage of critical systems | P2 |
| 8.17 Clock synchronization | ✅ | — | NTP evidence | P3 |
| 8.18 Privileged utility programs | 🟡 | — | Restrict and log | P3 |
| 8.19 Software installation | 🟡 | Change / Release | Allow-listing or admin restriction | P2 |
| 8.20–8.22 Network security, services, segregation | 🟡 | Infrastructure mgmt | Segmentation of production, finance, and corporate networks. Firewall rule reviews | P2 |
| **8.23 Web filtering** *(new)* | 🟡 | — | Evidence of filtering | P3 |
| 8.24 Cryptography | 🟡 | — | Crypto policy, key management | P2 |
| 8.25–8.31 Secure development lifecycle, testing, outsourced dev, environment separation | ❓ | Software dev / Release | **Depends on whether you build software.** If yes, P2. If not, these may be minimal | P2/P3 |
| **8.28 Secure coding** *(new)* | ❓ | — | As above | P2/P3 |
| **8.32 Change management** | ✅ | **Change enablement** | **Strong existing base.** Make sure security impact assessment is part of the change record and emergency changes are reviewed retrospectively | P2 |
| 8.33 Test information | ❌ | — | Ties to 8.11 masking | P2 |
| 8.34 Audit testing protection | ❌ | — | Plan audits to minimize disruption | P3 |

## Part 3: Where ITIL Gives You a Head Start

| Existing ITIL process | Annex A controls it can evidence | What to add |
|---|---|---|
| **Change enablement** | 8.32, 8.19, 5.8 (partial), Clause 6.3 | Security impact field, emergency change review, ISMS changes |
| **Incident management** | 5.24–5.28, 6.8 | Security classification, playbooks, forensics, regulatory notification, lessons learned |
| **Service configuration mgmt (CMDB)** | 5.9, 8.9 (partial) | Owners, classification, full in-scope coverage, reconciliation |
| **Deployment / release (patching)** | 8.8, 8.19 | Scanning, SLAs, exceptions, metrics |
| **Monitoring & event mgmt (SIEM)** | 8.15, 8.16, 5.7 | Retention policy, use-case catalogue, threat intel |
| **Problem management** | Clause 10.2 | Use for ISMS nonconformity root cause |
| **Service continuity** (if present) | 5.29, 5.30, 8.13, 8.14 | BIA, testing evidence |

You likely have **25–35% of the operational evidence** already in some form. The biggest gaps are the **management system itself** (Clauses 4–10), **risk assessment and treatment**, and **supplier management**.

---

# ISO 27001:2022 Readiness Pack (~250 staff, Financial Services)

**Note:** Tables paste directly into Excel when copied from the rendered view. Target dates use **M+n** (months from kickoff). Replace them with real dates once you set a start date.

---

## 1. Roadmap: Phases 2–3

### Phase 2: Implement Controls (M+3 to M+6)
- [ ] **Access control:** formalize joiner-mover-leaver, complete the first quarterly access review (privileged and financial systems), and enforce MFA everywhere in scope (A.5.15–5.18, 8.2, 8.5)
- [ ] **Supplier security:** due-diligence questionnaires for Tier 1 and 2 vendors, security clauses in new and renewing contracts, collection of SOC 2 or ISO certificates (A.5.19–5.23)
- [ ] **Vulnerability management:** authenticated scanning, remediation SLAs, exception register, pen test booked (A.8.8)
- [ ] **Incident management:** security classification, 3–5 playbooks (phishing, ransomware, data leak, account compromise, vendor breach), regulatory notification matrix, one tabletop exercise (A.5.24–5.28)
- [ ] **Business continuity and backup:** BIA, RTO/RPO, immutable backups, documented restore test, DR test (A.5.29, 5.30, 8.13)
- [ ] **Logging:** 12-month searchable plus long-term immutable archive live, with SIEM use cases documented (A.8.15, 8.16)
- [ ] **Change enablement:** add a security impact field and retrospective review of emergency changes (A.8.32)
- [ ] **Awareness:** annual training launched, phishing simulation running, completion tracked (A.6.3)
- [ ] **Classification:** scheme approved and applied to key repositories (A.5.12–5.13)
- [ ] **Configuration baselines:** CIS-aligned baselines for servers and endpoints (A.8.9)
- [ ] **Metrics:** monthly ISMS dashboard running to produce 9.1 evidence

**Exit criteria:** priority-1 controls operating with at least 2–3 months of records, and the SoA updated to reflect reality.

### Phase 3: Verify and Certify (M+6 to M+9)
- [ ] **Internal audit** of all clauses and in-scope controls by an independent or outsourced auditor (9.2)
- [ ] **Corrective actions** raised and tracked through problem management (10.2)
- [ ] **Management review** covering all 9.3 inputs, with minutes and decisions retained
- [ ] **Final SoA and risk treatment plan** signed off by risk owners, including residual-risk acceptance
- [ ] **Stage 1 audit** (documentation review), about M+7
- [ ] Close Stage 1 findings (allow 4–6 weeks)
- [ ] **Stage 2 audit** (effectiveness), about M+8 to M+9
- [ ] Close any minor nonconformities within the CB deadline. The certificate is typically issued 4–8 weeks after Stage 2.

**Ongoing:** annual surveillance audits, recertification every 3 years, plus a yearly internal audit and management review.

## 5. SIEM 90-Day Log Retention: Recommended Action

### Why change
ISO 27001 doesn't set a retention period, but your regulatory register will. Common financial-services drivers:
- **NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.6:** audit trails for detecting and responding to cybersecurity events must be kept **at least 3 years** (if you're NYDFS-regulated).
- **PCI DSS v4.0 (10.5.1):** **12 months**, with the most recent 3 months immediately available (if you handle card data).
- **DORA (EU) and GLBA Safeguards Rule:** require a documented logging and retention policy and activity monitoring, without one fixed period.
- Investigations often reach back 6–12+ months, since breaches are frequently found long after the initial intrusion.

**Confirm the applicable regimes with compliance or legal.** The default recommendation below satisfies most of them.

### What to change
1. **Logging standard** (A.8.15): define in-scope sources, events to capture, retention per tier, integrity controls, and access rules. Have compliance approve it.
2. **Retention tiers:**

| Tier | Period | Purpose | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hot (SIEM) | 90 days (unchanged) | Detection, triage | Existing SIEM |
| Warm (searchable) | 12 months | Investigations, PCI | SIEM long-term tier or data lake |
| Cold (archive) | 3 years (7 if counsel requires) | Regulatory, legal hold | Immutable object storage |

3. **Integrity and protection:** WORM/object lock (compliance mode), a separate cloud account or tenant, restricted access with no delete rights for SIEM admins, encryption, and hash or integrity verification.
4. **Source coverage:** confirm critical sources are forwarding (AD/Entra ID, firewalls, VPN, email, EDR, core banking and finance apps, privileged access, cloud audit logs), plus NTP sync (A.8.17).
5. **Restore test:** retrieve and search an archived log sample quarterly and record the result as evidence.
6. **Start the archive now.** Anything older than 90 days that isn't archived is permanently lost.

### Estimated costs and effort
Assumes about **20–50 GB/day** raw ingest for a 250-person organization, compressing roughly 8–10:1 for archive. Validate against your actual ingest.

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Cold archive (about 1–2 TB/yr compressed; e.g., S3 Glacier, Azure Archive) | About $100–$1,000/yr at 3 years retention |
| Warm searchable tier (vendor-dependent: Sentinel, Splunk, Elastic, etc.) | About $5k–$30k/yr; the biggest variable, so get a vendor quote |
| Engineering effort (design, pipeline, object lock, testing) | About 10–20 person-days |
| Policy and documentation | About 2–4 days |
| Ongoing operation (monitoring, quarterly restore tests) | About 1–2 days per quarter |
